recommendation: Keep the published source fix as-is. Any future redesign or relocation of registry/support tooling pages should remain a Product Director or work-group decision, but no additional core source change is needed for FHIR-25994.
issue_request: FHIR-25994 was Published/Persuasive for a non-substantive R5 correction to the FHIR registry tooling page. The Jira reported that the registry page had an outdated header/footer, a footer question-mark symbol, and missing/current-spec menu behavior; the accepted resolution was to make tooling pages outside the core specification visually distinct, use the proper logo, remove the search button, and adjust the footer.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged implementation commit for FHIR-25994 was found in local git history. The current source already had the FHIR logo header, an empty registry-specific nav area with no active search control, and a page-specific title/footer. The Jira's September 2022 comment said the build registry looked correct and the validator page was gone, and an untagged September 2022 commit adjusted the registry HL7 logo width, but the footer still contained a U+FFFD replacement character.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2020-05-11 assigned the issue to Grahame/Product Director because the page is under Product Director control rather than ordinary FHIR-I specification ownership. The static registry page is in current publish scope through publish.ini's [html] source=tools/html entry, and no tools/html validator page remains. Quoted Zulip and Confluence full-text searches found no additional conflicting community discussion.
reconciliation: Changed tools/html/registry/index.html to use the ASCII HTML entity © in the footer instead of the U+FFFD replacement character, preserving the existing registry-specific header/nav/footer treatment while removing the visible corrupted footer mark.
source_changes: tools/html/registry/index.html: replaced the corrupted U+FFFD footer character with the © HTML entity on the FHIR Implementation Registry page.
